title: Clarify and implement billing attribution for prefix / KV cache hits under batch aggregation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem summary: We have several customer reports and internal audits showing inconsistent usage charges when prefix caching and KV cache hits are in play together with request batching. Some customers see under- or over-charging compared to the actual GPU work performed. Root causes appear to be: (1) current metering counts tokens at the request-level before cache de-duplication and before batch aggregation, (2) batch aggregation then deduplicates prefixes/KV entries at execution time but metering has already recorded pre-dedup counts, and (3) when KV cache hits avoid compute work entirely the request-level token count is still contributing to quota/rate-limit checks incorrectly. This ticket defines the correct accounting rules and implements server-side changes to ensure billing matches compute and quota semantics.
proposed_solution: Bill based on effective compute tokens and attribute shared costs inside batches proportionally. Specifically: (A) Define three token metrics: requested_tokens (raw request prompt+gen length), compute_tokens (tokens that require model compute after prefix/KV cache elimination), and served_tokens (tokens delivered to the client). Billing and rate-limits should use compute_tokens for per-token charges and quota consumption. For batching, compute the batch_compute_total after dedup+cache elimination, then apportion that cost to each request by the request's compute_token share (if compute_token == 0 due to KV hit, it consumes zero compute quota). Log all three metrics for auditability. Implement a fallback safety mode where per-request requested_tokens are charged when compute_tokens cannot be reliably determined (grace period).
acceptance_criteria: Server emits compute_tokens, requested_tokens, and served_tokens in usage events for every request
Billing pipeline uses compute_tokens to generate invoiceable usage; comparable test invoices show defects fixed for previously reported customers
Quota enforcement and rate-limiting consult compute_tokens, preventing KV cache hits from consuming quota incorrectly
Batch-level tests demonstrate correct proportional attribution across at least 3 batch-size distributions (1, 4-8, 16+)
Audit dashboard updated: side-by-side view of requested vs compute vs served for top 100 customers
Backwards-safe: if compute_tokens unavailable, system uses requested_tokens but emits a migration audit flag
changes_required: Runtime: emit compute_tokens per request from executor after prefix/KV dedup stage
Metering pipeline: switch aggregation key to batch_compute_total and proportional attribution logic
Rate limiter: consult compute_tokens before decrementing quotas; add safe retries for zero-cost KV hits
Billing: use compute_tokens for invoice generation; mark any fallback events
Observability: add histograms for compute/request/served ratio and a daily report to billing dashboard
Docs/SDK: document new usage metrics and migration guidance for customers using raw token counts
rollout_plan: Spike (done) — measured delta between requested_tokens and compute_tokens across representative traffic (see updates)
Feature flag rollout: emit compute_tokens to events while billing still uses requested_tokens (2 days)
Metering switch behind flag with small customer cohort (5 customers) and manual invoice verification (1 week)
Gradual rollout to all customers with continuous monitoring for divergence and rollback criteria (CPU/GPU cost anomalies) (2 weeks)
Deprecate fallback after 60 days; notify customers and update invoices for historical corrections if necessary
updates: 2026-03-01: Issue created by Maya Chen summarizing audit findings and customer reports (ENG-6922, support cases #5543 and #5591)

2026-03-03: Spike completed by Diego Alvarez and SREs — analyzed 72h of traffic. Median requested_tokens - compute_tokens delta = 18%, P95 = 46%. KV-heavy workloads show compute_tokens == 0 in 12% of requests.
2026-03-04: Design review with PM (Arjun Singh) and Billing (Lena Park). Consensus: bill compute_tokens for fairness, but provide clear migration path and observable metrics.
2026-03-05: Prototype implemented in runtime executor to emit compute_tokens. PR opened: runtime/pull/1824. Initial tests show batch_compute_total calculation stable across sequence lengths.

2026-03-06: Billing team (owner: Lena Park) flagged invoice reconciliation complexity for month boundary cases. Follow-up: include per-event migration flags and allow backward adjustments within 30 days.

2026-03-08: Rate-limiter owner (Katherine Osei) reported potential denial-of-service vector if zero-cost KV hits are treated as free for quota — we added rule: zero compute_tokens still consume a minimal metadata quota token for abuse prevention. Decision written into spec.
2026-03-10: Added acceptance tests for proportional attribution (unit+integration). Preparing staged rollout; billing runbook drafted and reviewed by finance (PR: billing/pull/97).
